question: What is the prevalence of functional iron deficiency among US adults?
refined_question: Among noninstitutionalized US participants in NHANES 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic (Age >=18 years; Measured serum ferritin, transferrin saturation), what is the survey-weighted prevalence of functional iron deficiency (serum ferritin >=30 ng/mL with transferrin saturation <20%), overall and by sex, age group, and race and ethnicity?
title: Prevalence of Functional Iron Deficiency Among US Adults: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of NHANES 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic
hypothesis: Functional iron deficiency is common in this population and varies by sex, age group, and race and ethnicity.

pico.population: noninstitutionalized US participants in NHANES 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic (Age >=18 years; Measured serum ferritin, transferrin saturation)
pico.exposure: Not applicable (descriptive prevalence); subgroups: Sex, Age group, and Race and ethnicity
pico.outcome: Functional iron deficiency - ferritin >=30 ng/mL with TSAT <20%
pico.covariates: Sex, Age group, Race and ethnicity, Income-to-poverty ratio, Body mass index, Systemic inflammation (hsCRP >5 mg/L), and Chronic kidney disease (eGFR <60 or UACR >=30 mg/g)

outcome.label: Functional iron deficiency - ferritin >=30 ng/mL with TSAT <20%

model.rationale: Prevalence estimand: survey-weighted proportions with Korn-Graubard (beta) 95% CIs, overall and by subgroup, assessed against NCHS presentation standards; population counts from weighted totals. Adjusted correlates are estimated with survey-weighted quasi-Poisson regression (prevalence ratios).

missing_data.rationale: Complete-case primary analysis within the design; multiple imputation by chained equations as sensitivity analysis when covariates are missing.

benchmarks.label: Tawfik et al. 2024, US adults >=18 y, NHANES 2017-March 2020
benchmarks.population: Adults >=18 y with ferritin, iron and UIBC measured

benchmarks.label: Tawfik et al. 2024, US adults >=18 y, NHANES 2017-March 2020
benchmarks.population: Adults >=18 y with ferritin, iron and UIBC measured

rationale.statistician: Prevalence estimand: survey-weighted proportions with Korn-Graubard (beta) 95% CIs, overall and by subgroup, assessed against NCHS presentation standards; population counts from weighted totals. Adjusted correlates are estimated with survey-weighted quasi-Poisson regression (prevalence ratios).
rationale.epidemiologist: Correlates model includes Age, Sex, Race and ethnicity, Income-to-poverty ratio, Body mass index, Systemic inflammation (hsCRP >5 mg/L), and Chronic kidney disease (eGFR <60 or UACR >=30 mg/g) to describe independent associations with functional iron deficiency - ferritin >=30 ng/mL with TSAT <20%; these are descriptive, not causal, contrasts. Variables on the causal pathway or sharing laboratory components with the outcome/exposure are excluded to avoid over-adjustment.

limitations: Cross-sectional design: temporality cannot be established and associations must not be interpreted causally.
Single measurement of laboratory values; within-person variability and chronicity cannot be assessed.
Residual confounding by unmeasured or imperfectly measured factors (e.g., diet, medications, menstrual blood loss).
Self-reported comorbidities and behaviours are subject to recall and social-desirability bias.
NHANES excludes institutionalized and active-duty military populations.
Operational definition (Ferritin >=30 & TSAT <20%): TSAT uses the NHANES-reported value (LBDPCT); if absent it is computed as 100 x serum iron / TIBC.
